findings.finding: Eni's own July policy sets the special dividend mechanically: 100% of the CFFO increment if FY Brent > $90, or if gas or refining margins run >50% above budget. Sensitivities: EUR 0.11bn per $1 Brent, EUR 0.08bn per $1 SERM, EUR 0.03bn per EUR/MWh TTF. 9M Brent ran about $94, Brent is about $111 on 2026-10-22, and the FY SERM assumption is $14 vs a $6 budget, so the policy implies about EUR 0.64bn from refining alone plus roughly EUR 0.4-0.8bn from Brent above $90. Total about EUR 1.0-1.6bn, against a street expectation of about EUR 1bn (Equita, RBC, JPM capacity EUR 1bn / EUR 0.31 per share). The July text frames the October decision on the SERM sensitivity alone, which would give only EUR 0.64-0.8bn and disappoint, so the sign is net positive but two-sided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Base rate rebuilt from confirmed releases, because the baseline's 6-K history is not earnings. Eni rose on each of the last three capital-return upgrades: Q3 2025 (2025-10-24) buyback +20% to EUR 1.8bn, +2.5% Milan; Q1 2026 (2026-04-24) results missed (EUR 1.30bn vs 1.51bn) but the buyback went to EUR 2.8bn, about +1%; Q2 2026 (2026-07-29) beat (EUR 2.33bn vs 2.09bn) plus buyback to EUR 3.4bn, +4.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount has not been announced. The 2026-10-22 board release carried only the ordinary tranche. Street numbers range from EUR 0.4bn (JPM, July) to EUR 1bn (Equita/RBC/JPM October), and the policy arithmetic at the current Brent deck sits at or above the top of that range. If EUR 1.5bn were priced, the published estimates would sit there instead of at EUR 1bn and below.

findings.finding: Peers' Q3 2026 trading statements, published after Eni last spoke, put European refining margins at 2.5-4x Q2: TotalEnergies ERM $33.2 vs $13.5 in Q2, Shell indicative margin $42 vs $24, BP RIM $46.7 vs $29.6. Eni's own SERM was $8.3 in Q2 and $10.1 in Q1, and its FY assumption is $14, so a Q3 SERM around $20 is plausible. That supports the Refining line (Q2 adj EBIT EUR 80m) and the FY SERM that sizes the special dividend. Net of the rest: Brent fell from $104.5 in Q2 to about $91 in Q3, which costs E&P about EUR 0.3bn of quarterly CFFO, roughly offsetting the refining plus gas (TTF +~40% q/q) uplift. So the quarter lands near the EUR 2.48bn bar, not far above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Eni's earnings-line surprises have been out-voted by returns: a -14% net miss in Q1 2026 still closed about +1% on the buyback raise; +11% and +22% beats in Q2 2026 and Q3 2025 went with +4.5% and +2.5%, both alongside buyback raises.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company-compiled consensus (EUR 2.48bn, above Q2's 2.33bn at a higher Brent) already embeds a refining uplift. What is not pinned down is Eni's Q3 SERM print itself, which no peer statement gives, and whether Eni lifts the FY SERM above $14. That feeds finding 1's special-dividend size.

findings.finding: The FY 2026 CFFO guide of EUR 15bn was set on Brent $85 / SERM $14 / TTF EUR 50. With 9M Brent about $94 and Q4-to-date about $105-111, FY Brent runs around $95-97: about +EUR 1.1-1.3bn of CFFO at EUR 0.11bn per $1, before gas. Policy sends 60% of increments up to $90 to buybacks, and JPM forecasts the FY buyback at EUR 4bn vs EUR 3.4bn. Gearing is already about 10% (Q2) and Plenitude's deconsolidation removes about EUR 3bn of net debt. A raised CFFO guide plus a buyback top-up is the default path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance and buyback raises came with every positive Eni print reaction in the last year: +2.5% (Q3 2025), about +1% (Q1 2026, CFFO guide +20% to EUR 13.8bn), +4.5% (Q2 2026, CFFO to EUR 15bn, buyback to EUR 3.4bn).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sell-side expects the raise (Equita calls EUR 15bn conservative; Barclays sees larger EPS upgrades than peers). Not priced is the size. The guide still formally reads $85 Brent while spot is about $111, and the stock's average target (about EUR 26.1) sits below spot, so published targets have not caught up with a $95+ FY deck.

JPM EUR 4bn buyback: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/jpmorgan-sees-strong-q3-for-eu-oil-and-gas-favors-these-major-stocks-4938263 (2026-10-08). Shares the Brent deck and the policy document with finding 1; they are separate capital lines (buyback/CFFO guide vs special dividend).

findings.finding: Eni put a voluntary price cap on its Enilive retail network from 2026-09-28 (petrol EUR 1.99/l, diesel EUR 2.19/l, about 17 cents under market), for 30 days with a possible extension to 2026-12-31. Equita estimates the cost at EUR 85-100m a month. It is framed in the Italian press as the alternative to a windfall tax on extra profits. Any extension or cost disclosure on the 2026-10-23 call is a Q4 cash drag that could be netted against the special dividend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Eni print carried a price-cap disclosure; no history on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: The cost is unquantified by Eni ('non sappiamo quanto costa né a quale condizione finisce', quotidiano.net). At EUR 85-100m a month through December it is about EUR 0.3bn, about 0.4% of market cap, so a small drag; a priced cap would show up as cuts to Q4 estimates, which no preview mentions.

findings.finding: Positioning is crowded long into the print. The ADR is at its 52-week high (+7.6% over 20 days), the Milan line hit a record EUR 26.695 on 2026-10-20 and is up about 52-60% YTD, and the average analyst target (about EUR 26.1) sits below spot. The special dividend (about EUR 1bn) and a buyback raise are the published expectation, so the bar for a positive reaction is a return package above about EUR 1bn plus a buyback raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Eni still rose on its Q2 2026 print after a strong run, but that run was smaller. No confirmed Eni print in the last year sold off on a return increase.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself rather than a hidden fact. It is filed so the panel sees that much of the good news is already in a stock at its high: RisparmiOggi (2026-10-19) says the 60% YTD rise may already price in the good news.

findings.finding: BofA (2026-10-16) sits below consensus on the reported perimeter: Q3 adj EBIT EUR 3.5bn vs a 'VA consensus' of EUR 3.8bn (-8%) and adj net about EUR 2.5bn vs EUR 2.6bn (-3%), because the Searah JV (Eni-Petronas, Indonesia/Malaysia) does not contribute to consolidated EBIT. The headline EBIT line could therefore read as a miss even if pro-forma (5.69bn) and net land in line. CFFO EUR 4.6bn in line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 headline net miss (-14%) was looked through on the buyback raise (about +1%).
findings.why_not_priced: One broker's perimeter point. The company-compiled bar is pro-forma (EUR 5.69bn) and includes JVs, so a consolidated-EBIT 'miss' headline is possible on wires that print the consolidated line.

findings.finding: Portfolio cash supports bigger returns. The Q2 release lists a $2bn Ares/PIMCO upstream partnership with cash expected in Q3, binding sales of 10% of the Indonesian Searah-operated assets to Pertamina and Medco on 2026-10-12, a pending 10% Baleine sale and a planned 10% Kutei stake sale in 2026, plus Plenitude's EUR 1.56bn capital increase and deconsolidation from 2026-10-01 (about -EUR 3bn net debt, -3.5pp leverage). What the money buys: it takes gearing below the 10-15% target floor and frees room for a larger buyback or special without stretching the balance sheet.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Eni's dual-exploration/satellite disposals have historically been folded into buyback raises rather than moving the print alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely known individually, but the Q3 net-debt print (first after the Ares cash) and the pro-forma gearing after Plenitude have not been shown. A sub-10% gearing number would make a EUR 1bn+ special plus a buyback top-up look easy.
